text.p: Cobra Electronics Corp, which reported cost reductions resulted in a profitable 1996, said Friday it expects continued profitability.
"We feel we are well-positioned for growth and continued profitability in 1997," said Jerry Kalov, president and chief executive, in a statement.

Cobra, which designs and makes consumer electronics prodicts, reported a 1996 fourth quarter profit of $490,000 or $0.08 a share compared with a loss of $750,000 or $0.12 in the same quarter a year ago. Sales rose to $24.3 million from $23.8 million in the fourth quarter of 1995.

For the year ended December 31, 1996, Cobra reported a net profit of $601,000 or $0.10 compared with a net loss of $1.1 million or $0.18 for the 1995 year. Sales for 1996 were $90.3 million compared to $90.4 million in 1995.

Gross margin for the year was 18.1 percent compared with 18.3 percent a year ago. Selling, general and administrative expense as a percentage of sales dropped to 15.9 percent in 1996, from 17.8 percent in 1995, the company said.
"We made solid progress in 1996 and achieved our goal of returning to profitability," said Kalov.

Cobra had reported a 1996 first quarter loss due to a weak retail environment that subsequently improved. Following the first quarter loss, it reported three consecutive profitable quarters and generated $1.2 million of net income during the last nine months of 1996.
Improved results reflect cost reductions and substantial investments in expanding product distribution and development, it said.

Kalov noted the company recently added Circuit City as a customer and will increase its product offerings with Sears in 1997. In addition, Cobra said its patent-pending SoundTracker noise reduction technology will be incorporated into much of its 1997 CB product line.

Kalov also said Cobra will introduce in 1997 a Safety Alert traffic warning detector that warns motorists of fast-moving emergency vehicles, roadside hazards and approaching trains via signals. It will also introduce in 1997, a Family Radio Service two-way radio.
"These are two new market segments for us," said Kalov in a year end financial statement.
